title: lat_long_interaction
hypothesis: Latitude and Longitude individually map weakly to median_house_value, but their interaction (Latitude * Longitude, plus quadratic terms Lat^2 and Lon^2) captures California's diagonal coastal-to-inland price gradient that neither raw coordinate explains alone.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: high novelty vs queue (geographic interaction, not a ratio feature); strong signal — listed in GOAL.md obvious wins; expected to capture coastal/inland clustering missed by raw lat/lon.

title: house_age_bucket
hypothesis: HouseAge has a non-linear relationship with median_house_value: very old neighborhoods (>40y) and very new developments command different premiums than middle-aged stock. Ordinal bucketing into 4-5 age bins should outperform a single linear coefficient.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: novel categorical-bucketing approach distinct from ratio/log features in queue; signal from GOAL.md; captures non-linear age-price curve a linear baseline cannot.

title: coastal_distance
hypothesis: California's coastal premium is large but not captured by raw Latitude or Longitude alone. A derived feature approximating distance-to-coast (e.g., Longitude shifted relative to the coastal meridian ~ -124.0 W, or a piecewise distance taking Latitude into account for the coastal arc) should explain a large fraction of price variance unexplained by raw coordinates.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: high novelty — opens a geographic-derivation axis distinct from lat_long_interaction (polynomial). Strong signal: CA coastal premium is one of the largest known drivers of median_house_value. Cheap to implement (single derived column).

title: winsorize_heavy_tails
hypothesis: AveRooms, AveBedrms, AveOccup, and Population have heavy right tails with extreme outliers (e.g., AveRooms > 100, AveOccup > 1000 in a few rows) that wreck OLS by dragging the fit. Winsorizing these columns at the 99th percentile (or capping to a fixed threshold) should improve baseline R² with no new feature semantics — pure preprocessing orthogonal to ratio/log/interaction families.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: highest novelty — opens a preprocessing axis the queue has zero coverage in. Medium-high signal: heavy tails on AveOccup/AveRooms are documented in this dataset and disproportionately damage OLS. Cheap to implement (per-column quantile cap).

title: medinc_quadratic
hypothesis: Income-to-price has diminishing returns at the high end and a steeper slope in the mid-range. Adding MedInc^2 alongside MedInc captures the concave/luxury bend that a linear coefficient misses — distinct from log_median_income because polynomial expansion can be U-shaped and is symmetric in interpretation rather than monotone-concave.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: medium novelty — same input column as log_median_income but a different non-linear form (polynomial vs concave-monotone). Medium signal: complementary to log_median_income, not a substitute. T2 because closest queue-neighbor (log_median_income) is already T1.
